Verdict

There is insufficient evidence to conclude a malicious supply-chain compromise, but an import-time path that may start a remote control worker is present. **Overall risk: medium**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

  • **medium — import-time automatic execution path**

- At the end of puvinoise/__init__.py, the package runs code immediately on import:

python

try:

ensure_control_worker_started()

except Exception:

pass

- Based on the function and exported API names (start_agent_control_worker, AgentControlWorker, ControlCommand), this appears related to starting a remote control or polling worker.

- The deterministic pre-scan also identified network request and subprocess.run(...) paths in agent_runtime/agent_control_worker.py, suggesting that importing the package may start a path capable of polling for commands and executing processes.

- However, the body of ensure_control_worker_started() was not included in the provided text, so the actual default behavior and activation conditions require further verification.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • No malicious install-time evidence was shown for setup.py, .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, or PEP 517 build hooks.
  • Ordinary console_scripts are user-triggered and are not treated as malicious automatic execution here.
  • Confirmed automatic execution evidence:

- puvinoise/__init__.py calls ensure_control_worker_started() at import time.

- The broad exception suppression (except Exception: pass) may hide failures from the user.

- Whether this actually starts a remote control worker depends on the implementation in bootstrap.py, which was not provided.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • **Credential harvesting**

- No evidence was shown of broad discovery of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, npm/PyPI/GitHub tokens, wallets, or other developer secrets.

- The package reads PUVINOISE_API_KEY and .puvinoise/agent_<id>.json, but this appears to be documented SDK state/authentication usage rather than malicious credential harvesting.

  • **Exfiltration / staging**

- agent_autoregister.py sends runtime metadata (sdk_version, runtime, entrypoint, pid, host) to /api/agent-register and heartbeat endpoints.

- This is described as SDK registration/telemetry behavior, and the provided evidence is insufficient to classify it as malicious exfiltration.

- No evidence was shown of broad file collection, archive staging, and upload.

  • **Persistence**

- atexit.register(stop_heartbeat_loop) and a daemon heartbeat thread are process-lifetime cleanup/background behavior.

- No evidence was shown of systemd units, cron jobs, shell profile modification, launch agents, startup folders, or reboot persistence.

  • **Lateral movement**

- No evidence was shown of Kubernetes service-account token use, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, CI token theft, or GitHub Actions workflow injection.

  • **Obfuscation / loader**

- No clear evidence was shown in the provided text of base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec-based staged loaders, self-deleting droppers, or stealth payloads.

- The pre-scan mentioned eval(expr), but the relevant source body was not provided, so this is insufficient to classify as a malicious loader.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on the provided text, there is no confirmed evidence of hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, wheel/sdist mismatch, sudden dependency insertion, or typosquatting.
  • Comments in sidecar_manager.py describe auto-downloading a sidecar binary and including platform-specific binaries in wheels.

- This is explained as part of the SDK sidecar design and is not, by itself, malicious supply-chain evidence.

- The actual artifact contents and whether downloaded binaries are hash/signature verified require further review.

Further Verification Needed

  • Inspect puvinoise/bootstrap.py, especially ensure_control_worker_started():

- whether it starts the remote control worker by default on import

- whether it requires explicit opt-in or has opt-out controls

- which endpoint it polls

  • Inspect puvinoise/agent_runtime/agent_control_worker.py:

- whether remote commands can lead to arbitrary shell/subprocess execution

- whether command authentication or signature verification exists

  • Compare sdist and wheel artifacts:

- whether sidecar binaries are included

- whether binary hash/signature verification is enforced

- whether execution behavior differs between sdist and wheel

  • The current assessment is limited by the partial extracted text and pre-scan leads.
